Resolution path: case_169 -> style_id linework_coloring_elastic_pressure_cool_nocturne_soft_two_band_controlled_rim_complete_line_color -> test_ids P7000505 (seed 1001), P7000506 (2002), P7000507 (3003) in tests/reports/phase7_linework_coloring_v2/runs/<id>/image_01.png (all 1024x1024). I viewed all three full frames plus 2x-4x crops of the collar/lapel/shoulder-seam and sleeve-fold strokes.

What full resolution shows:
- Seed 2002 (P7000506): the collar/lapel strokes are unmistakably pressure-modulated. The upper collar edge facing the light runs as a hairline, and the same stroke swells to a heavy weight where the collar folds over and meets the shoulder, ending in a blunt loaded terminal at the collar tip; the collar-tip stroke going down-left starts as a hairline and thickens as it descends into the fold.
- Seed 3003 (P7000507): the lapel line enters at the shoulder as a hairline and gradates continuously thicker down to the lapel notch, thickest exactly at the notch/fold corners where the fabric gathers, then continues heavy down the lapel break. The mirrored collar line does the same.
- Seed 1001 (P7000505): this is the seed that read as "near-uniform hairlines" at 256px, and that is the artifact. The garment strokes here are few and delicate, but at 4x each sleeve-fold stroke visibly begins as a broken near-invisible hairline in the lit green-teal plane and swells to a distinctly heavier stroke as it runs down into the shadowed fold; the shoulder silhouette also carries more weight on the shadow side. Thin-to-thick within a single stroke, correctly correlated with weight/shadow versus light.

So the specific unsettled question — whether the thin collar/shoulder lines thicken around weight and narrow around light — resolves in favour of the item on every seed; there is no seed disagreement, only a density difference (1001 simply has fewer garment strokes to read, which is what flattened at thumbnail scale). The reviewer already granted cool_nocturne (indigo shadows, blue-green midtone skin, warm nose/lip note) and soft_two_band; controlled_rim is also present as the warm rust rim confined to the shadow-side shoulder silhouette.

Saturation was not the concern, but I checked tests/reports/phase7_linework_coloring_v2/saturation_screen.json for completeness: the cool_nocturne group (43 items, median 0.1909, range 0.1663-0.2319) reports outlier_count 0, so nothing flags there either.

Quantitative note for honesty: I also ran a pixel-level stroke-width script (local-median darkness mask, skeleton + distance transform) against crisp_uniform and fine_tapered controls. That metric was not discriminative — it picks up soft_two_band shading boundaries as well as pen strokes, and the crisp_uniform controls scored equal or higher width variance. I am therefore basing the verdict on direct visual inspection of the full-resolution strokes, not on that metric.
